title: What If You Stood in the Fastest Wind Ever Recorded?
subject: tropical cyclone

scenes.text: What if you stood in the fastest wind ever measured? No hurricane comes close.
In 1996, a station on Barrow Island, Australia, recorded a gust of 253 miles an hour.
It came from Tropical Cyclone Olivia, and an unmanned instrument caught it.
Before that, the record was 231 miles an hour, set on Mount Washington in 1934.
Three men on the summit timed it by stopwatch while ice built up on the building.
No U.S. hurricane has topped 190 miles an hour. That gust was stronger than any of them.

description:
